title: Not changing the work
hook: holiness isn't a new job; it's the same work for a new reason, and the week comes back
tomorrow: what did Lawrence do the moment he failed?

segments.voice: Yesterday, an omelette turned in the pan, and a neighbor's word about offering every act. Your line was for love of God. Today Lawrence says what that means for your whole job.
screen: `FOR LOVE OF GOD.` → `NOW, THE WHOLE JOB.`

segments.voice: Career quizzes. Find-your-passion podcasts. The daydream of quitting everything to open a bakery by the sea. A lot of advice about meaning starts with changing the job. Brother Lawrence, who spent years at a stove he didn't love, has a different starting point, and it fits in one sentence. He said it to his visitor plainly, and it turns the bakery daydream inside out.
screen: `FIND YOUR PASSION.` → `THE BAKERY BY THE SEA.` → `ONE SENTENCE.`

segments.voice: In the fourth conversation, Lawrence says our sanctification, our becoming holy, doesn't depend on changing our works. It depends on doing for God's sake what we usually do for our own. Same dishes, same errands, same desk. Only the reason moves. That isn't a rule against ever changing jobs. It's a claim about where holiness lives. His own life is the proof. In the second conversation he admits he naturally disliked kitchen work. He got used to doing everything there for the love of God, asking for grace to do it well, and he found, he says, that it all became easy. Saint Paul says it in the Douay-Rheims: "whether you eat or drink, or whatsoever else you do, do all to the glory of God." Now the week comes back. Thérèse's last words: my God, I love you. A doctor who never left her convent. The little way: small things, great love. Then Lawrence. Spring will come, from a bare tree. He broke everything, and was welcomed. For love of God, even an omelette. Each one makes the same move: the work stays, the reason changes.
screen: `NOT CHANGING OUR WORKS.` · `FOR GOD, WHAT WE DO FOR OURSELVES.` · `HIS KITCHEN: DISLIKED, THEN EASY.` · `SIX LINES FROM THIS WEEK.` · then, large: `SAME WORK, NEW REASON.`

segments.voice: On a scrap of paper, write one task you'd rather not do tomorrow: the commute, the dishes, the report. Next to it, write a new reason, for God, or for someone you love. Fold it, keep it in your pocket, and rest while the sit runs.
Not changing the work. Lawrence's rule for a holy life: the same tasks, done for God's sake instead of our own.
Your line: same work, new reason. The kitchen stayed; the reason changed. Have a good week.

howItsDone: Many Catholics speak of offering up their ordinary work, and readers of Brother Lawrence take his kitchen as the model: the same tasks, done for God.

fork.setup: your dad hates his long commute and is thinking of taking a pay cut just to switch jobs. what would Lawrence ask first?

fork.reveal: Lawrence doesn't forbid a new job. he says holiness doesn't depend on one: do for God's sake what you'd usually do for your own.
